content.text: {"screening_id":"SCR_000024","question_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 3, Section 2.8 Randomization and blinding","evidence_summary":"Participants were assigned using balanced-block randomization with variable-size, computer-generated blocks of two, four, or six and a 1:1 allocation ratio.","rationale":"A computer-generated allocation sequence with randomly varying block sizes is an appropriate random method.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.2","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.4 and 2.8","evidence_summary":"Randomization occurred after informed consent and was performed electronically through the Castor EDC data-management system.","rationale":"Central electronic assignment after enrolment probably concealed upcoming allocations, although the paper does not explicitly describe who could access the sequence or the technical concealment safeguards.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Pages 3–4, Results and Table 1","evidence_summary":"The groups were described as generally balanced, but the empagliflozin group was older on average and had somewhat shorter surgery and cardiopulmonary-bypass durations. Other important baseline characteristics, including kidney function, diabetes, procedure type, and EuroSCORE II, were similar.","rationale":"Some differences occurred in this small pilot trial, but they are plausibly attributable to chance and do not provide compelling evidence that randomization failed. Older age in the intervention group would not obviously explain its lower AKI incidence.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.1, 2.3, and 2.8","evidence_summary":"The study was explicitly open-label; the intervention group received empagliflozin, while the control group received no intervention rather than a placebo.","rationale":"Participants would have been aware whether they received the study medication.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.2","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 3, Section 2.8 Randomization and blinding","evidence_summary":"The authors state that patients, care providers, and study personnel were not blinded to treatment allocation.","rationale":"Carers and intervention providers were aware of assigned intervention.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.3–2.4; Page 3, Results","evidence_summary":"All 25 analyzed intervention participants started empagliflozin three days before surgery. The paper does not report important nonadherence or trial-context-induced departures from the assigned interventions.","rationale":"Although complete adherence through postoperative day two is not documented in detail, there is no indication of material deviations caused by the trial context.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.3–2.4; Page 3, Results","evidence_summary":"No material trial-context-induced deviations from intended intervention were identified.","rationale":"This question is not applicable because relevant deviations were not identified.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.5","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.3–2.4; Page 3, Results","evidence_summary":"No material trial-context-induced deviations requiring an assessment of balance were identified.","rationale":"Balance of deviations is not applicable when no relevant deviations were identified.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.6","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 3, Sections 2.9 Statistical analyses and 3 Results","evidence_summary":"The authors state that analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population, consisting of 25 assigned to empagliflozin and 30 assigned to control, with patients analyzed in their assigned groups.","rationale":"Analysis by randomized assignment is appropriate for estimating the effect of assignment to intervention.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.7","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Page 3, Results, participant flow description","evidence_summary":"Five of 60 randomized patients were excluded before intervention and surgery: one withdrew consent, two surgeries were cancelled, and two procedures changed from on-pump to off-pump surgery. The remaining 55 were analyzed in their assigned groups.","rationale":"Strict intention-to-treat inclusion of all randomized participants was not achieved, but four excluded participants did not undergo the target surgery and therefore could not experience postoperative AKI as defined. There is no indication that exclusions differed because of post-randomization renal outcomes, so material impact is unlikely.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Pages 3–4, Sections 3 and 3.2 Kidney injury; Figure 2","evidence_summary":"The AKI result accounts for all 55 participants in the stated analysis population: 5/25 in the empagliflozin group and 20/30 in the control group.","rationale":"Outcome data appear available for all participants included in the analysis population.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.2","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 3–4, Sections 3 and 3.2","evidence_summary":"No missing AKI outcomes are apparent among the 55 analyzed participants.","rationale":"A separate demonstration that missingness did not bias the result is unnecessary because outcome data were available for all or nearly all analyzed participants.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.3","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 3–4, Sections 3 and 3.2","evidence_summary":"No missing AKI outcomes are apparent among analyzed participants.","rationale":"Dependence of missingness on the true outcome is not applicable when relevant outcome data are not missing.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 3–4, Sections 3 and 3.2","evidence_summary":"No missing AKI outcomes are apparent among analyzed participants.","rationale":"This question is not applicable because relevant outcome missingness was not identified.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.1","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.4 and 2.6 Outcomes","evidence_summary":"AKI within seven days was defined using KDIGO 2012 criteria based on serum creatinine and urine output. Creatinine was measured daily and urine output hourly while a urinary catheter remained in place.","rationale":"KDIGO criteria are an established and appropriate method for measuring postoperative AKI.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.2","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.4 and 2.8; Pages 4–5, Sections 3.2 and 4","evidence_summary":"The trial was open-label. Creatinine was measured daily, but hourly urine-output monitoring continued only until urinary-catheter removal on ICU discharge. The combined AKI result was driven substantially by urine-output criteria; creatinine-only AKI incidence in the control group was reported as 27% rather than 66.7% using full KDIGO criteria.","rationale":"Because ICU discharge and catheter-removal timing may be influenced by unblinded clinical management, the duration and completeness of urine-output ascertainment could differ between groups. The paper does not report safeguards ensuring equivalent seven-day urine-output ascertainment.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.3","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 3, Section 2.8 Randomization and blinding","evidence_summary":"Study personnel and care providers were not blinded, and no separate blinded adjudication of AKI was reported.","rationale":"Those recording clinical measurements or determining whether KDIGO criteria were met were likely aware of treatment assignment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.4","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, Sections 2.4 and 2.8; Pages 4–5, Sections 3.2 and 4","evidence_summary":"AKI thresholds were objective, but urine-output ascertainment depended on catheterization and ICU monitoring, and the intervention group had a numerically shorter ICU stay. The paper indicates that urine-output criteria substantially increased the observed AKI incidence.","rationale":"Knowledge of assignment could influence clinical decisions about fluid management, diuretics, ICU discharge, or catheter removal, potentially affecting whether urine-output-based KDIGO criteria were observed.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.5","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Pages 2–5, Sections 2.4, 2.8, 3.2, and 4","evidence_summary":"No direct evidence of differential measurement or deliberate outcome classification is reported. AKI was determined using numerical creatinine and urine-output thresholds.","rationale":"Despite a plausible route for influence through unblinded care and monitoring duration, the objective KDIGO thresholds make substantial direct assessor influence less likely. Residual concern remains because urine-output ascertainment was tied to clinical management.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.1","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Page 3, Sections 2.7 Sample size and 2.9 Statistical analyses","evidence_summary":"The planned sample size was 80 participants. AKI incidence was examined after 25%, 50%, and 75% inclusion, and trial leadership stopped enrolment at approximately 75% because of the observed between-group AKI disparity. No independent data safety board, formal statistical stopping boundary, or adjustment for repeated interim examination is reported.","rationale":"The analyzed sample size and timing of the AKI analysis were determined after unblinded AKI data had been examined. The paper does not establish that the reported analysis followed a fully prespecified plan protected from data-dependent decisions.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.2","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Page 3, Section 2.6 Outcomes; Pages 4–5, Section 3.2 and Figure 2","evidence_summary":"AKI incidence within seven postoperative days according to KDIGO criteria was explicitly listed as a secondary outcome. The paper also considered creatinine and urine-output criteria separately and AKI stages.","rationale":"The combined KDIGO measure and seven-day window were specified in the methods, making selection from alternative outcome definitions less likely, although several related AKI measurements were available.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.3","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Page 3, Sections 2.7 and 2.9; Pages 4–6, Sections 3.2, 4, and 5","evidence_summary":"The investigators repeatedly examined between-group AKI incidence and stopped at a favorable interim result without a reported statistical stopping rule or multiplicity adjustment. AKI could also be analyzed using combined KDIGO criteria, creatinine alone, urine output alone, and different AKI stages.","rationale":"The reported estimate was obtained at a data-dependent stopping point selected after repeated unblinded inspection. This creates a substantial possibility that the presented numerical effect reflects selection of a favorable analysis time or dataset, even though the basic KDIGO outcome was prespecified.","agent_confidence":"High"}],"domain_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"The computer-generated, variable-block sequence was appropriate, and electronic assignment probably concealed allocation. Baseline differences are compatible with chance in a small pilot trial and do not compellingly indicate randomization failure."},{"domain_id":"D2","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"Participants and providers were unblinded, but no important trial-context-induced deviations were identified. The 55 participants who underwent the target surgery were analyzed according to assignment; exclusion of five pre-intervention participants is unlikely to have materially affected the postoperative AKI result."},{"domain_id":"D3","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"The reported AKI counts account for all 55 participants in the stated analysis population, with no apparent missing outcome data."},{"domain_id":"D4","provisional_domain_judgement":"Some concerns","domain_rationale":"KDIGO criteria are appropriate and largely objective, but the trial was unblinded and urine-output monitoring depended on ICU catheterization. Because urine-output criteria drove much of the high AKI incidence and monitoring duration could be affected by unblinded clinical decisions, differential ascertainment cannot be excluded."},{"domain_id":"D5","provisional_domain_judgement":"High","domain_rationale":"The trial was stopped below its planned sample size after repeated unblinded examinations showed a large AKI difference, without a reported formal stopping boundary or multiplicity-adjusted analysis. The resulting estimate is therefore vulnerable to data-dependent selection and exaggeration at a favorable interim look."}],"agent_overall_provisional_judgement":"High","agent_overall_rationale":"The overall provisional judgement is High because of high risk in selection of the reported result arising from unblinded, outcome-dependent early termination after repeated interim examination of AKI incidence. There are additional concerns about unblinded ascertainment of an outcome substantially dependent on urine-output monitoring, although randomization, deviations from intervention, and missing outcome data otherwise appear reasonably handled."}
